records.name: Wagner Free Institute of Science
records.summary: A free natural history museum and science education institution in North Philadelphia, founded in 1855, with a Victorian-era specimen hall of more than 100,000 items and regular talks and courses.
records.what_you_do: Visit the museum for free and walk through the specimen hall, come to a Weeknights at the Wagner talk or the First Saturday Open House, take an evening course, or join as a member.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Friday, 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. The first Saturday of the month is open noon to 4 pm, but the site gives two different season ranges for that Saturday, so check before a visit. Closed on some holidays and breaks.

cost.text: Admission is free. The institute prefers that you register on its Eventbrite page, but walk-ins are welcome.

access.notes: The museum is on the second floor and reached by a flight of stairs; the visit page does not mention an elevator. Accessibility questions go to info@wagnerfreeinstitute.org. Nearest SEPTA stop named on the visit page: Temple University / Cecil B. Moore Avenue on the Broad Street Line (local trains only).

first_step.how: Register for a free visit on the institute's Eventbrite page, or walk in during museum hours, Tuesday to Friday.
first_step.basis: The visit page says walk-ins are welcome, that scavenger hunts guide first-time visitors, and that staff are available to answer questions.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is self-guided: you walk through the specimen hall at your own pace past fossils, minerals, and mounted animals. A themed scavenger hunt is one way to start, and staff can answer questions. Admission is free, and the institute also runs adult talks and evening courses.
first_visit_tips: Register on the Eventbrite page first, since it speeds entry; walk-ins are also welcome.
Check the hours before you go, because the first Saturday schedule is listed two different ways.
The museum is up a flight of stairs, so ask info@wagnerfreeinstitute.org about access before you come.
Pencils and paper are available for sketching in the hall.

records.notes: The visit page does not state an admission fee; the cost comes from the homepage, which says admission is free. Tier 1 said visits are booked in advance, but the visit page says registration is preferred and walk-ins are welcome. The October 22, 2026 talk is a dated event and is recorded only as last sign of life.

records.name: Weavers Way Co-op
records.summary: A member-owned food co-op in Northwest Philadelphia with a Farm Market that the public can shop. Members help run the store by volunteering their time.
records.what_you_do: Shop the Farm Market, join as a member, or sign up for a working membership to help out in the store.

schedule.text: Farm Market open Tuesday and Friday 11 am to 7 pm, and Saturday 10 am to 4 pm.

locations.label: Farm Market, at W.B. Saul Agricultural High School

cost.text: Shopping the Farm Market does not require membership. Membership asks for a member equity investment that is refunded if you leave the Co-op; the amount is not listed on the pages we read.

first_step.how: Visit the Farm Market during its hours and shop without joining. To become a member, use the Join Now button on the membership page.
first_step.basis: The Farm Market is open to anyone without membership, and the membership page explains how to join through a Join Now button. The site does not describe a newcomer session.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Farm Market is open to the public, so you can walk in during its hours and shop without joining. Members get extra perks, such as a 5 percent discount on Weavers Way Farms produce and member-only sales. Fees are not listed on the pages we read, so call the Farm Market before you join.
first_visit_tips: Check the hours first: Tuesday and Friday 11 am to 7 pm, Saturday 10 am to 4 pm.
The site links a parking map rather than describing parking, so look at it before you drive.
Call 267.876.3101 with questions about membership before you sign up.
If you join, a working member owes six volunteer hours per person each year (anyone over 16), due in the first four months.

records.notes: Status is probably_active, not active: the pages we read have no dated events, so the last_sign_of_life month is carried over from tier 1 and was not confirmed on this pass. Working membership hours are an annual requirement for members, not for shoppers.

records.name: Wednesday Night Rides
records.summary: A social bike ride in Philadelphia held about every other week. Each ride is labeled easy, standard, or adventurous, and each has its own posted route and start point.
records.what_you_do: Show up for a posted ride that fits your comfort level, and follow the group for the next one.

schedule.text: Rides about every other week. Each ride lists its own start point and route.

locations.label: Start point posted for each ride

cost.text: Rides are free and voluntary, and no waiver is required.

requirements.gear: A front white headlight and a rear red reflector or tail light after dark, a bike kept in good repair, and a basic repair kit with a spare tube. Bring water in summer and warm layers in winter.

first_step.how: Pick a posted ride on wednightrides.org, check its start point and route, and show up with lights and a bike in good shape.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome regardless of experience, and every ride is posted in advance with a start point and route, so a newcomer knows where to show up.
first_step.what_to_expect: A ride is a group trip through Philadelphia on a posted route, with rides running roughly 6 to 9.5 miles, some of them hilly. Each ride post names a start, a route, and an end spot, often a park or a brewery. Riders are asked to follow traffic rules, stop at red lights, and look out for pedestrians.
first_visit_tips: Read the ride post for the start point and route before you go, since they change from ride to ride.
After dark, bring a white front light and a red rear light or reflector, which Pennsylvania law requires.
Bring a basic repair kit, water in summer, and warm layers in winter.
Arrive sober, and stay to the right and out of the way of traffic.

records.notes: The site does not define the easy, standard, and adventurous levels, and it does not say whether you need to sign up for a ride. Ride dates on the homepage run into late September 2026; the homepage does not say which are upcoming.

records.name: West Park Cultural Center
records.summary: An arts nonprofit in West Philadelphia that runs after school art, dance, theater and guitar classes for young people, plus summer camps and a yearly outdoor arts festival.
records.what_you_do: Sign a child up for an after school class or a summer camp. Anyone can come to the June West Park Arts Fest. Adults can volunteer, donate, or shop at the gift shop.

schedule.text: After school classes run during the school year, and Camp Ginkgo runs in the summer. Class days and times differ by program, so check each program page. The visual art class meets Tuesday and Thursday, 4 to 5:30 pm.

cost.text: Class fees are not listed on the pages we read. Ask the center about fees and any financial help when you register.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the program pages and use its Register now or Learn more link, or call 215-473-7810 to ask about class times and fees.
first_step.basis: Programs and the June Arts Fest are open to the public, and each program page has a way to register. The site does not describe a beginner program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Afterschool classes meet during the school year, and the visual art class for ages 10 to 13 meets Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4 to 5:30 pm at Martha Washington School. Fees differ by program, so ask before you sign up. Volunteers for the ceramics class must have criminal and child abuse clearances.
first_visit_tips: Call or email ahead to confirm class times, since not every program page lists them.
Ask about fees and financial help when you register.
Go to the June Arts Fest first to see the center's work before you sign up.

records.notes: The volunteer page footer shows a 2023 copyright, which is not evidence of current activity; the June 13, 2026 Arts Fest on the homepage is the dated evidence. The clearance requirement applies to the ceramics tutoring volunteer role only; the page does not say it applies to other volunteer roles. Camp Ginkgo details and the other afterschool class schedules were not confirmed on the program pages.

records.name: West Philly Bizarre
aka: West Philly Bizarre of CultureTrust Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit makers market that gives local artists, crafters, and culture creators low-cost or free places to sell, mostly for West Philadelphians from underserved communities.
records.what_you_do: Shop or sell at the Clark Park market on select Saturdays, take a workshop such as the spring nail class, or apply as a vendor. The site says it puts Southwest and West Philly residents first at Clark Park.

schedule.text: Clark Park market on select Saturdays, April through November, held outdoors. Pop-ups and workshops are announced on the events calendar.

cost.text: Visiting the market is open to the public. A vendor pays an application fee of $0 to $10, then a daily fee of $15 for one table at Clark Park, or about $25 for a 10 by 10 space. Workshops cost about $45 each.

first_step.how: Visit the Clark Park market on a select Saturday from April to November, or sign up for the newsletter to hear when vendor applications open.
first_step.basis: The market is open to anyone, and the vendor page explains how applications work through Marketspread, with walk-up spots first come, first served.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Clark Park market runs outdoors on select Saturdays, April through November, with no rain dates. Nothing is provided for vendors there, so sellers bring their own tables, racks, chairs, and tents. Shoppers can browse and buy from local makers.
first_visit_tips: Check the events calendar for the Saturday market dates, since they are announced there.
If you plan to sell, read the vendor page first. Applications run through Marketspread, and Clark Park applications were closed when we checked.
Bring your own shade and seating if you plan to sell, because nothing is provided at Clark Park.
Vendors with financial hardship can write to market@westphillybizarre.com.

records.notes: The vendor page does not describe a priority system; the local priority comes from the site's general statement. Clark Park applications were closed when checked and usually open in late winter, and the site gives no reopening date. The May 31 nail workshop is a dated event and is recorded only as last sign of life.

records.name: William Way LGBT Community Center
records.summary: The LGBT community center in Center City. A core group of volunteers helps run its programs, from peer counseling and recovery meetings to the archives and library.
records.what_you_do: Staff the front desk, table at events, give tours, help with fundraisers, or join a regular shift or committee such as the arts committee or the archives.

schedule.text: Community Mondays run monthly on Monday evenings, 6 to 8 pm: game night, an open mic, and a craft night. Volunteer shifts are weekly, with monthly planning meetings.

locations.label: St. Luke's and the Epiphany (game night and craft night)

cost.text: Volunteering is free. The Community Mondays page does not list a fee, so check before you come.

first_step.how: Come to Community Mondays game night on the first Monday at St. Luke's and the Epiphany, or add your name to the Volunteer Mailing List for one-time roles.
first_step.basis: Game night says all are welcomed and is described as low stakes, and the volunteer page explains how to sign up for one-time roles and regular shifts.
first_step.what_to_expect: Community Mondays are evening events for LGBTQIA+ adults 18 and up: board and card games at game night, an open mic for LGBTQIA+ performers, and a monthly craft night. The page does not say how many people come or whether you need to register, so plan on the 6 to 8 pm window.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-732-2220 to confirm the date and whether you need to sign up.
Bring a game of your own if you want to play one in particular; bringing your own games is allowed.
Go to the volunteer page if you want to help; one-time roles need only a mailing list sign-up.

records.notes: The site does not state minimum age for volunteers, required training, background checks, or building access. The Community Mondays events are listed for LGBTQIA+ adults 18 and up. Dated Monday events from spring 2026 are recorded only as last sign of life.

records.name: Work to Ride
records.summary: A horsemanship program for young people in Philadelphia, based at the Chamounix Equestrian Center in Fairmount Park. It runs a summer camp and one-day farm and horse programs for kids. The group says its riding is free for under-resourced youth.
records.what_you_do: Kids learn horsemanship and equine sports; volunteers help with programs at the stables.

schedule.text: Summer camp runs in one-week sessions through the summer, with dates posted each year on the camp page. Riding camp is for ages 8 to 13, a little kids camp for ages 5 to 7, and polo camp for ages 8 and up. Other programs run on a schedule the group announces.

cost.text: The group says its riding is free for under-resourced youth, and scholarships are available. Summer camp costs $525 per one-week session for riding and little kids camps, and $275 for polo camp.

first_step.how: Email wtr@worktoride.net or call (215) 877-4419 to ask about the next session, or fill in the volunteer form if you are over 14.
first_step.basis: The site lists a phone number, an email address, a camp registration form, and a volunteer form, so the way in is clear. It does not describe a join process for youth.
first_step.what_to_expect: Camp days run 9 am to 4 pm, with lunch from 12 to 1. Campers do barn chores, learn about animal care and safety, ride twice a day, and explore Fairmount Park, with games and arts and crafts. Groups of about five rotate through stations with the same counselor all week.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the age range and session dates before you register, since the site lists them in more than one way.
Plan for a full day, 9 am to 4 pm.
Camp fees are not refundable, and changing weeks costs $10 if space allows.
Registration is not complete until payment is made; you can pay by card over the phone or by check.

records.notes: Sources disagree on the camp age range: the homepage says ages 7 to 13, and the camp page says ages 5 to 13 with a little kids camp for ages 5 to 7. The camp page's 2026 date table is blank and shows 2027 dates, so confirm session dates with the group. Volunteers must be over 14. The street address is not stated on the pages we read. No accessibility details are given.

notes: Tier 2 deep pass for batch 08 (7 groups). Each group got up to about four or five page reads, plus two WebSearch calls for West Park and Work to Ride, which returned only older cached snippets; those snippets were checked against the group sites before use where possible. The Work to Ride camp fees and ages are from the camp page itself. West Park class fees, other afterschool class schedules, and Camp Ginkgo details are not confirmed. No partner groups were named on these sites that were worth a lead. Budget not exhausted; no blocked pages.
